method: A read-only script replicating outdoor-feature-candidates.py gate for gate, writing nothing, attributing every one of the 1,281,126 features to the FIRST gate it fails.
hypothesis_tested: 91,068 non-trail outdoor features carry 2 or more attributes yet appear in neither _feature-candidates nor _aggregate-only-features, so a gate defect is silently discarding entities that meet the stated bar. Birnhorn (AT peak, Wikidata Q683611, ele 2634, prominence 1659) was the worked example.
verdict: LARGELY REFUTED. The gate chain is sound. I raised this as a defect of the same class as the 1,314,927 unattributable POI and it is not one.
why_the_hypothesis_was_wrong: I counted attributes and assumed 2 or more attributes meant the entity met the bar. It does not. The bar is three gates, not one: NOTABLE (a Wikidata item or a Wikipedia article), MEASURABLE (a number or a practical fact), and PARENT (a containment polygon). 67,474 of the 91,068 are camp sites (31,417) and caravan sites (13,035) whose two attributes are a website and a phone number and which carry no encyclopedia entry at all. A campsite with a phone number is a directory listing, not a page, and the NOTABLE gate is the reason this inventory is not a business directory.

the_genuinely_recoverable_group.composition: 904 peaks, 234 mountain huts, 45 wilderness huts, 24 caves, 10 viewpoints and the remainder scattered. Birnhorn is one of the 904.
the_genuinely_recoverable_group.cause: The parent layer holds no polygon between 0.05 and 20,000 km2 that covers the point, so the feature cannot be placed in a hierarchy a reader recognises.
the_genuinely_recoverable_group.fix: Extend the parent layer where it is sparse, NOT relax the parent gate. A page that cannot say where the thing is has not earned its place.
the_genuinely_recoverable_group.honest_size: 6,527 is the ceiling on this recovery, against the 91,068 I first reported. I am correcting my own figure by a factor of 14.

note_on_the_40123: notable_but_no_fact_a_reader_came_for is the 40,123 that hold a Wikidata item or a Wikipedia article and no number and no practical fact. These are the real enrichment target, and they are the measured version of the 55,173 figure I quoted from attribute counting alone.
